findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The amount-cap pass holds on the quoted figures: GBP 1300 per calendar month gives annual rent of GBP 15,600 (1300 x 12), and five weeks is 15,600 / 52 x 5 = GBP 1,500. The GBP 1,500 deposit is exactly at the cap, not above it. Nothing in the contract contradicts that amount or suggests the rent and deposit cover different tenancies or shares, so there is no basis to dismiss. The pass stays limited by unresolved scope facts. Jurisdiction and tenancy type are unknown, and the contract gives a London address but does not say it is an ordinary private tenancy rather than an excluded arrangement. This only concerns the amount. It says nothing about deposit protection, authenticity, or the representative's authority. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants
